title: Printing and export to PDF from a desktop app
when: Users of the desktop app need to print a report or invoice and save it as a PDF file, with clean page breaks and no app chrome on paper.
prompt:
Goal: A print view with print CSS, a Print command and a PDF export path that works on each OS, with the per OS limits written down.
Steps:
1. Build the printable content in a dedicated <article id="print-view">; @media print hides everything else (toolbar, sidebar, dialogs).
2. @page { size: A4; margin: 15mm } with a setting for Letter; break-inside: avoid on rows and cards; thead { display: table-header-group } to repeat headers.
3. Print command calls window.print(); test it per OS, since some WebViews ignore it.
4. PDF export option A: the OS print dialog offers save as PDF on most systems; tell the user so in the Export menu.
5. Option B, when print is not available: write the print view to a standalone report.html in the temp folder with inlined CSS, then open it with Neutralino.os.open so the default browser prints it.
6. Option C, a direct PDF: generate it in a worker with a small vendored PDF library, then save with showSaveDialog and filesystem.writeBinaryFile.
7. Use black text, real borders instead of background colors, and tabular figures for numbers.
Quality bar:
- No buttons or menus appear on paper.
- Tables split between rows, never through a row.
Pitfalls:
- Background colors that do not print by default.
- Assuming window.print works the same in every WebView.
Verify:
- [ ] @media print and @page rules exist.
- [ ] The Print command has a fallback path.
- [ ] Exported files open in a PDF viewer.
Output: print.css, print.js and the Export menu items.

examples.input: imprimir o relatório do app desktop e salvar em PDF
examples.output: print.css with @page A4, window.print with report.html fallback opened via os.open, optional PDF writer
